{"kind":"tool","id":"gWsvwC1lp5A","toolName":"write_file","input":{"path":"supabase/migrations/20261028000400_client_access.sql","content":"-- Formivo: client invitations and form-level client permissions.
-- Security requirements (PRD §13):
--   * invitation tokens are stored only as hashes
--   * a form has at most one ACTIVE client permission (partial unique index)
--   * acceptance is performed by the transaction-safe app_private.accept_client_invitation

create table public.client_invitations (
  id uuid primary key default gen_random_uuid(),
  form_id uuid not null references public.forms (id) on delete cascade,
  invited_email text not null
    check (invited_email = lower(btrim(invited_email)) and char_length(invited_email) between 3 and 254),
  token_hash text not null unique check (char_length(token_hash) >= 32),
  status text not null default 'pending' check (status in ('pending', 'accepted', 'revoked', 'expired')),
  invited_by_user_id uuid not null references auth.users (id),
  expires_at timestamptz not null,
  accepted_by_user_id uuid references auth.users (id),
  accepted_at timestamptz,
  revoked_at timestamptz,
  created_at timestamptz not null default now(),
  constraint client_invitations_expiry check (expires_at > created_at),
  -- An accepted invitation always records who accepted it and when.
  constraint client_invitations_accepted_invariant check (
    (status = 'accepted' and accepted_by_user_id is not null and accepted_at is not null)
    or status <> 'accepted'
  )
);

-- At most one active (pending) invitation per form and email.
create unique index client_invitations_pending_form_email_uniq
  on public.client_invitations (form_id, invited_email)
  where status = 'pending';

create index client_invitations_form_id_idx on public.client_invitations (form_id);
create index client_invitations_email_idx on public.client_invitations (invited_email);
create index client_invitations_expires_at_idx on public.client_invitations (expires_at);

create table public.form_client_permissions (
  id uuid primary key default gen_random_uuid(),
  form_id uuid not null references public.forms (id) on delete cascade,
  client_user_id uuid not null references auth.users (id) on delete cascade,
  invitation_id uuid references public.client_invitations (id),
  granted_at timestamptz not null default now(),
  revoked_at timestamptz,
  created_at timestamptz not null default now()
);

-- One row per (form, client); re-granting reactivates the existing row.
create unique index form_client_permissions_form_user_uniq
  on public.form_client_permissions (form_id, client_user_id);

-- PRD §13.10: at most one ACTIVE client account per form, enforced in the database.
create unique index form_client_permissions_active_form_uniq
  on public.form_client_permissions (form_id)
  where revoked_at is null;

create index form_client_permissions_user_idx on public.form_client_permissions (client_user_id);
create index form_client_permissions_form_idx on public.form_client_permissions (form_id);
"}}

  before update on public.subscriptions
  for each row execute function public.set_updated_at();

create table public.usage_periods (
  id uuid primary key default gen_random_uuid(),
  workspace_id uuid not null references public.workspaces (id) on del [… 96 characters omitted] sion_count integer not null default 0 check (submission_count >= 0),
  created_at timestamptz not null default now(),
  updated_at timestamptz not null default now(),
  constraint usage_periods_window check (period_end > period_start),
  constraint usage_periods_workspace_window_unique unique (workspace_id, period_start, period_end)
);

create trigger usage_periods_set_updated_at
  before update on public.usage_periods
  for each row execute function public.set_updated_at();

  payload_hash text,

  created_at timestamptz not null default now(),
  constraint webhook_events_provider_event_unique unique (provider, provider_event_id)
);

-- destructive operations). Never store raw tokens, passwords or full payloads.
create table public.audit_logs (
  id uuid primary key default gen_random_uuid(),
  actor_user_id uuid references auth.users (id) on delete set null,

{"kind":"tool","id":"gW5fcV4JF0o","toolName":"write_file","input":{"path":"supabase/migrations/20261028000600_functions.sql","instructions":"Phase 2 migration: app_private helpers and transaction-safe RPCs","content":"-- Formivo: authorization helpers and transaction-safe privileged functions.
--
-- Helpers (has_role, is_workspace_owner, owns_form, can_view_form) are called from
-- RLS policies, so they are SECURITY DEFINER (they read tables whose own RLS would
-- otherwise recurse) and executable by API roles.
--
-- Privileged functions are executable by the service role only. They are never
-- exposed through PostgREST because the app_private schema is not in the exposed
-- schema list, and EXECUTE is revoked from anon/authenticated as defense in depth.
-- The server performs its own authorization before calling them (PRD §8, §19).

create schema if not exists app_private;

grant usage on schema app_private to anon, authenticated, service_role;

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- RLS helpers
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

create or replace function app_private.has_role(p_role text)
returns boolean
language sql
stable
security definer
set search_path = ''
as $$
  select exists (
    select 1
    from public.account_roles r
    where r.role = p_role
      and r.user_id = auth.uid()
  );
$$;

create or replace function app_private.is_workspace_owner(p_workspace_id uuid)
returns boolean
language sql
stable
security definer
set sea [… 9,002 characters omitted] text default null
)
returns jsonb
language plpgsql
volatile
security definer
set search_path = ''
as $$
declare
  v_form public.forms%rowtype;
  v_usage_id uuid;
  v_count integer;
  v_submission_id uuid;
begin
  if p_form_id is null or p_period_start is null or p_period_end is null then
    raise exception 'INVALID_ARGUMENTS';
  end if;

  if p_data is null or jsonb_typeof(p_data) <> 'object' then
    raise exception 'INVALID_PAYLOAD';
  end if;

  select * into v_form
  from public.forms f
  where f.id = p_form_id;

  if not found then
    raise exception 'FORM_NOT_FOUND';
  end if;

  if v_form.status <> 'active' then
    raise exception 'FORM_PAUSED';
  end if;

  insert into public.usage_periods (workspace_id, period_start, period_end)
  values (v_form.workspace_id, p_period_start, p_period_end)
  on conflict (workspace_id, period_start, period_end) do nothing;

  select up.id into v_usage_id
  from public.usage_periods up
  where up.workspace_id = v_form.workspace_id
    and up.period_start = p_period_start
    and up.period_end = p_period_end;

  -- Locked increment: concurrent requests serialize here, so the limit cannot
  -- be bypassed and one submission can never be double counted.
  update public.usage_periods up
  set submission_count = submission_count + 1
  where up.id = v_usage_id
    and up.submission_count < coalesce(p_max_submissions, 2147483647)
  returning up.submission_count into v_count;

  if v_count is null then
    raise exception 'SUBMISSION_LIMIT_REACHED';

  insert into public.submissions (form_id, data, source_origin)
  values (p_form_id, p_data, p_source_origin)
  returning id into v_submission_id;

  return jsonb_build_object(
    'ok', true,
    'submission_id', v_submission_id,
    'usage_count', v_count,
    'usage_limit', p_max_submissions
  );
end;
$$;

revoke execute on all functions in schema app_private from public, anon, authenticated;
grant execute on function app_private.initialize_developer_account(uuid, text, text, text) to service_role;
grant execute on function app_private.accept_client_invitation(text, uuid, text, integer) to service_role;

--
-- Model:
--   * developers see only data whose ownership path leads to their workspace,
--   * clients see only forms with an ACTIVE permission for their user id,
--   * roles, invitations, usage, billing writes and audit logs are service-role only,
--   * every table has RLS enabled; tables without policies are service-role only.
--
-- Policies target the `authenticated` role. The `anon` role gets no access to
-- application tables (the public submission endpoint uses the service role from
-- the server). The service role bypasses RLS and must authorize explicitly.

alter table public.profiles enable row level security;
alter table public.account_roles enable row level security;
alter table public.workspaces enable row level security;
alter table public.forms enable row level security;
alter table public.submissions enable row level security;
alter table public.client_invitations enable row level security;
alter table public.form_client_permissions enable row level security;
alter table public.subscriptions enable row level security;
alter table public.usage_periods enable row level security;
alter table public.webhook_events enable row level security;
alter table public.audit_logs enable row level security;

-- profiles: read and update your own profile only. Profile rows are created by
- [… 1,887 characters omitted]  authenticated
  using (app_private.owns_form(id))
  with check (app_private.owns_form(id));

create policy forms_delete_owner
  on public.forms for delete
  to authenticated
  using (app_private.owns_form(id));

-- submissions: developers manage submissions of their own forms; clients read
-- submissions of shared forms. Inserts only ever happen through the public
-- submission endpoint (service role), so there is no insert policy.
create policy submissions_select_viewer
  on public.submissions for select
  to authenticated
  using (app_private.can_view_form(form_id));

create policy submissions_update_owner
  on public.submissions for update
  to authenticated
  using (app_private.owns_form(form_id))
  with check (app_private.owns_form(form_id));

-- No delete policy: submissions are archived, not destroyed (PRD §12.6).

-- client_invitations: developers read invitations for their own forms.
-- Creation, resend and revocation go through trusted server logic only, because
-- tokens and lifecycle transitions must be handled transactionally.
create policy client_invitations_select_owner
  on public.client_invitations for select
  to authenticated
  using (app_private.owns_form(form_id));

-- form_client_permissions: the client sees their own (active) grants; the
-- workspace owner sees grants on their forms. Writes are service-role only.
create policy form_client_permissions_select_self_or_owner
  on public.form_client_permissions for select

    or app_private.owns_form(form_id)
  );

create policy form_client_permissions_update_owner
  on public.form_client_permissions for update
  to authenticated
  using (app_private.owns_form(form_id))
  with check (app_private.owns_form(form_id));

-- subscriptions / usage_periods: read-only for the workspace owner.
-- Billing writes happen exclusively through verified webhooks (service role).
create policy subscriptions_select_owner
  on public.subscriptions for select
  to authenticated
  using (app_private.is_workspace_owner(workspace_id));

create policy usage_periods_select_owner
  on public.usage_periods for select

import path from "node:path";

const MIGRATIONS_DIR = path.resolve("supabase/migrations");

/** Supabase-equivalent bootstrap that must exist before our migrations run. */
const SUPABASE_SHIM_SQL = `
do $$
begin
  if not exists (select 1 from pg_roles where rolname = 'anon') then
    create role anon nologin;
  end if;
  if not exists (select 1 from pg_roles where rolname = 'authenticated') then
    create role authenticated nologin;
  end if;
  if not exists (select 1 from pg_roles where rolname = 'service_role') then
    create role service_role nologin bypassrls;
  end if;
end

create schema if not exists auth;

create table if n [… 1,242 characters omitted] new PGlite();
  await db.exec(SUPABASE_SHIM_SQL);

  for (const file of migrationFiles()) {
    const sql = readFileSync(path.join(MIGRATIONS_DIR, file), "utf8");
    try {
      await db.exec(sql);
    } catch (error) {
      throw new Error(`Migration failed: ${file}\n${(error as Error).message}`, { cause: error });
    }

/** Creates an auth user row exactly as Supabase Auth would (id + email only). */
export async function createUser(db: PGlite, email: string): Promise<string> {
  const result = await db.query<{ id: string }>(
    `insert into auth.users (email) values ($1) returning id`,
    [email],
  );
  const id = result.rows[0]?.id;
  if (!id) throw new Error("failed to create test user");
  return id;
}

/**
 * Runs `fn` with the request JWT set to `userId` and the `authenticated` role
 * active, so RLS policies evaluate exactly as they would for a signed-in user.
 */
export async function asUser<T>(
  db: PGlite,
  userId: string,
  fn: () => Promise<T>,
): Promise<T> {
  await db.query(`select set_config('request.jwt.claims', $1, false)`, [
    JSON.stringify({ sub: userId, role: "authenticated" }),
  ]);
  await db.query(`set role authenticated`);
  try {
    return await fn();
  } finally {
    await db.query(`reset role`);
    await db.query(`select set_config('request.jwt.claims', '', false)`);
  }
}

/** Runs `fn` as the service role (bypasses RLS, as the server-side admin client does). */
export async function asServiceRole<T>(db: PGlite, fn: () => Promise<T>): Promise<T> {
  await db.query(`set role service_role`);
  try {
    return await fn();
  } finally {
    await db.query(`reset role`);
  }
}

/** Asserts that an async call rejects with a machine-readable error code. */
export async function expectErrorCode(
  call: Promise<unknown>,
  code: string,
): Promise<void> {
  try {
    await call;
  } catch (error) {
    const message = error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error);
    if (message.includes(code)) return;
    throw new Error(`expected error code ${code}, got: ${message}`);
  }
  throw new Error(`expected error code ${code}, but the call succeeded`);
}

export async function selectAll<T>(db: PGlite, sql: string): Promise<T[]> {
  const result = await db.query<T>(sql);
  return result.rows;
}

import { createServerClient } from '@supabase/ssr'
import { NextResponse, type NextRequest } from 'next/server'

export async function proxy(request: NextRequest) {
  let response = NextResponse.next({ request })
  const supabase = createServerClient(url, anon, { cookies: { getAll: () => request.cookies.getAll(), setAll: (c) => { c.forEach(...) request + response cookies } } })
  const { data: { user } } = await supabase.auth.getUser()
  // optimistic redirects
  const path = request.nextUrl.pathname
  const isProtected = path.startsWith('/dashboard') || ... 
  if (!user && isProtected) → redirect /login?next=
  if (user && isAuthPage) → redirect '/' (optimistic; layout does role resolution)
  return response with refreshed cookies
}
export const config = { matcher: [...] }
```

export function sanitizeNextPath(raw: unknown): string | null {
  if (typeof raw !== 'string') return null;
  const value = raw.trim();
  if (!value.startsWith('/')) return null;
  if (value.startsWith('//') || value.startsWith('/\\')) return null;
  if (value.includes('://')) return null;   // extra safety
  return value;
}

export type PostAuthInput = {
  requestedNext?: string | null; // already-validated next  inviteToken?: string | null;
  roles: readonly Role[];
};
export function pickPostAuthPath({requestedNext, inviteToken, roles}: PostAuthInput): string {
  const next = sanitizeNextPath(requestedNext);
  if (next) return next;
  if (inviteToken) return `/invitations/${inviteToken}`;
  if (roles.includes('developer')) return '/dashboard';
  if (roles.includes('client')) return '/client';
  return '/';
}
```
